# GENERATED FILE - do not hand-edit the pins below the marker.
#
# Pinned dependency versions for the deployed simulator venv, derived from
# pylock.toml by scripts/lock_dependencies.py.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# --------------------
# The EC2 bootstrap (infra/simulator-ec2-alb/scripts/user_data.sh) rebuilds the
# Python venv FROM SCRATCH on every instance replacement -- and because the
# instance is configured with `user_data_causes_replacement=True`, that happens
# on any user-data or repo-asset change, i.e. most deploys.
#
# Every runtime dependency in pyproject.toml is an open lower-bound range
# (`fastapi>=...`, `pydantic>=...`, ...), so without pinning, the deployed code
# runs against whatever those resolve to on the day the instance happens to be
# built. On 2026-07-31 that bit us: a fresh instance resolved `mcp>=1.0.0` to
# **mcp 2.0.0**, which moved `mcp.server.fastmcp` to `mcp.server.mcpserver`. The
# app crash-looped on import and the ALB target never went healthy -- while
# CloudFormation reported UPDATE_COMPLETE and systemd reported the service
# `active`. Nothing in the repo had changed to cause it.
#
# pip applies this as a CONSTRAINTS file (`-c`), so it only restricts which
# versions may be chosen -- pyproject.toml still decides WHICH packages are
# installed. Pins for packages the deployed venv never installs (the `dev` and
# `docs` extras) are therefore inert here; they are included so this file is an
# exact projection of pylock.toml with no filtering rule to get wrong.
#
# WHERE VERSIONS COME FROM
# ------------------------
# pylock.toml (PEP 751) is the SOURCE OF TRUTH. This file is a projection of it
# for pip, which cannot install from a pylock.toml. Do not edit pins here: an
# edit would be silently overwritten on the next regeneration, and would make
# this file disagree with the lock that scanners read.
#
# HOW TO CHANGE A VERSION
# -----------------------
#   scripts/lock_dependencies.py                        # idempotent; keeps pins
#   scripts/lock_dependencies.py --upgrade              # move everything
#   scripts/lock_dependencies.py --upgrade-package mcp  # move one package
#
# Re-running without a flag is a no-op: `uv pip compile` preserves the versions
# already in pylock.toml, so picking up new versions is always an explicit,
# reviewable act rather than a side effect of regenerating.
#
# Then REDEPLOY so a real instance proves the new set boots before it is
# trusted. A version set that resolves is not a version set that runs -- the
# 2026-07-31 outage resolved perfectly.
#
# tests/test_dependency_lock.py fails if this file and pylock.toml disagree.
#
# Pin lineage: originally captured 2026-07-31 from i-02ce6a6905e0f13d7 (healthy,
# serving traffic; Python 3.12 / aarch64 / AL2023), then adopted as the seed for
# pylock.toml. Subsequent changes flow from the lock, not from a live instance.
# --- BEGIN GENERATED PINS - do not edit below this line ---
